selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to think about at the beginning?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to think about a short example that helps explain why the world exists, why human beings were created, and the secret of the daily prayers.

questions.question: Who is the main person in the comparison?
questions.answer: A powerful king.

questions.question: What kinds of things did the king own?
questions.answer: He owned great treasures, hidden riches, amazing skills, deep knowledge, and many kinds of learning.

questions.question: Why did the king want to open a display?
questions.answer: He wanted to show his beauty, excellence, power, wealth, art, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is the first way the king wanted to see his own perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it himself directly.

questions.question: What is the second way the king wanted to see his own perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it through how others looked at it.

questions.question: What does the king’s wish to display his treasures and skills tell us about him?
questions.answer: It shows that he wanted what was inside him to become known and seen.

questions.question: Which is more than money in the king’s possessions: only jewels, or jewels plus knowledge and skill?
questions.answer: Jewels plus knowledge and skill.

questions.question: How do we know the king was not ordinary?
questions.answer: He had many treasures, hidden wonders, unusual arts, and wide knowledge.

questions.question: What lesson can a student infer from the two “respects” mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: Goodness and beauty can be appreciated personally and also recognized through the understanding of others.

questions.question: What title is given at the start of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The Eleventh Word.

questions.question: What holy words come before the explanation begins?
questions.answer: The passage begins in the name of Allah and then gives verses that point to signs in creation.

questions.question: Name three things from creation mentioned in the verses.
questions.answer: The sun, the moon, and the earth.

questions.question: What human part is mentioned along with the sky and the earth?
questions.answer: The self, or soul.

questions.question: After the verses, what does the reader get invited to do?
questions.answer: To reflect on a brief comparison.

questions.question: What subjects does that comparison help explain?
questions.answer: The purpose of the world, the creation of human beings, and the meaning of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: In the comparison, what did the king have besides visible treasures?
questions.answer: He also had hidden treasures and inner excellences like skill and knowledge.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that people with beauty and perfection want to see and show it?
questions.answer: To help explain why the king wanted to prepare a public display.

questions.question: What did the king hope people would notice in his display?
questions.answer: His rule, wealth, artistic skill, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is one main message from the ending of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The king wanted his perfection to be witnessed in two ways: by himself and by others.

questions.question: What kind of example is used to teach the lesson in this passage?
questions.answer: A story-like comparison about a king.

questions.question: What was special about the king’s stored wealth?
questions.answer: It included many precious gems and other hidden wonders.

questions.question: What else made the king great besides wealth?
questions.answer: His mastery in arts, his broad knowledge, and his deep learning.

questions.question: What did the king prepare so people could see what he had?
questions.answer: A place of display, like an exhibition.

title: 11 Word Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose
